baseline_facts.content: Patient is thirty two years old.
Patient experiences intermittent fatigue lasting a couple of days.
Patient experiences pins and needles in the right hand.
Patient has episodes of numbness in the right hand.

A colleague observed the patient walking slightly differently during episodes.
Abnormal gait episodes last three to four days.
Symptoms began probably a month and a half, maybe two months ago.

Currently, episodes occur a couple of times a day.
The patient sometimes feels nauseous.
The patient generally feels weak.
The patient sometimes does not feel like doing anything.
The patient has no current difficulty swallowing.
During episodes, the patient feels like there is something in the throat.
The patient has no difficulty speaking during episodes.
The patient does not think they have visual problems during episodes.
The patient wears glasses.
In the last couple of days, during episodes, the patient cannot hold a cup of coffee.
In the last couple of days, during episodes, drinking coffee is slightly harder.
The patient's father underwent a neck operation to reduce stroke risk.
The patient had a blood test for cholesterol that was fine.
The patient was checked for diabetes and it was OK.
The patient's blood pressure was checked and it was OK.
The patient has no history of mini-strokes.
The patient reports no other illnesses.
The patient takes an Aspirin, seventy five milligrams, once a day.
The patient started Aspirin after his father had his operation.
The patient takes Aspirin because of something he read on the internet.
The patient is allergic to penicillin only.
The patient does not smoke.
The patient works as a medical doctor in plastic surgery.
The patient lives with his wife.
The patient had no symptoms at the time of consultation.
The working diagnosis is mini-stroke or transient ischemic attack.
A referral to a TIA clinic was sent during the consultation.
The TIA clinic is expected to contact the patient within one to two days.
The TIA clinic will perform an ultrasound of the carotid arteries.
The TIA clinic might perform a brain scan.
The patient was advised to attend A&E if symptoms return and are prolonged.
Abnormal gait is not present outside of episodes.
Pins and needles are always in the right hand.
